name: Admin & Platform Management
description: Platform-level admin capabilities: tenant/workspace management, support tooling, feature flags, plan enforcement, global defaults (AI providers, notification providers), incident response actions, and auditability.
goals: Operate a production multi-tenant SaaS safely.
Provide support tooling without violating tenant isolation.
Centralize feature flags and progressive rollouts.
Provide immutable audit trails for privileged actions.
nonGoals: Replacing a full CRM/support suite (integrate with external tools where needed).

rules: Platform admins can access limited tenant data via audited support sessions.
Every privileged action must record workspace_id (if applicable) and platform_admin user_id.
Support tooling must prefer metadata views over raw content views; require explicit escalation for sensitive data.

actors.name: Super Admin
actors.description: Highest privilege platform admin; can provision/disable other admins and assign role templates.

actors.name: Platform Admin
actors.description: Operates the SaaS across all tenants using least-privilege templates.

actors.name: Support Admin
actors.description: Customer support tooling via scoped support sessions.

actors.name: Security Admin
actors.description: Security incident tooling and policy operations.

actors.name: System
actors.description: Applies feature flags, plan policies, and admin actions.

workflows.name: Provision Platform Admin (Super Admin)
steps: Super Admin creates an admin invite and selects role template IDs.
System enforces MFA setup at first login and records an immutable audit entry.
Super Admin may later grant/revoke templates; all changes are audited with before/after.
Disabled admins immediately lose access to /v1/admin/* endpoints.

workflows.name: Audited Support Session
steps: Platform admin requests temporary support session for a workspace.
System validates reason and assigns least-privilege scope with expiry.
All actions performed under support session are logged to audit.
Session auto-expires and cannot be extended without creating a new session.

controls: Separate platform admin auth realm (MFA mandatory, IP allowlists recommended).
Platform admin authorization is permission-based using system role templates (no role-name bypass).
All privileged actions logged immutably with before/after states.
Support sessions are time-bounded and scoped.
No direct DB access for routine support operations; use audited APIs.

logs: Platform admin action audit log stream

acceptanceTests: Only Super Admin can invite/disable platform admins and assign role templates; all changes are audited.
Support sessions expire automatically and cannot be used afterward.
Feature flag changes take effect without redeploy and are auditable.
Platform admin endpoints require MFA-backed auth and are rate limited.
